content.title: Dialogue with Trypho
content.author: Justin Martyr (d. c. 165) · Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (1885), tr. Marcus Dods and George Reith
content.note: Justin's account, written about 155–160, of a debate with a Jew named Trypho over whether Jesus is the Christ of the Scriptures. It records the Jewish reading of Isaiah 7:14 as 'young woman', applied to Hezekiah (chapters 43, 67, 71). For the earliest recorded Jewish–Christian exchange on messianic prophecy. Public domain translation; the held copy is CCEL's electronic text.
content.read: Held in this project's corpus: CCEL's text export sources/library/source-patristic-ccel/anf01.txt. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 7): chapters 43, 66, 67 and 71 read for virgin-birth and messianic-prophecy. Described, not quoted. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 7): chapter 69 ('a magician, and a deceiver of the people') also read for trilemma; that phrase quoted.

publicDomain.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 1, translated by Marcus Dods and George Reith (1885)
publicDomain.basis: The held CCEL text of the 1885 American edition (Buffalo: Christian Literature, 1885): published before 1931, so public domain in the US; Dods d. 1909 (Reith's death year not confirmed, so worldwide status is unconfirmed).
